levels.name: First words
levels.sentenceLengthHint: strictly max 7 words per sentence, simple subject-verb-object
grammarAllowed: present of ser and estar (soc, ets, és, estic, està)
definite and indefinite articles (el, la, els, les, un, una) with correct apostrophation before a vowel (l'home, l'aigua)
regular plurals (-s, -es) and adjective agreement in gender and number
present indicative of first-conjugation -ar verbs (parlo, parles, parla)
simple questions with què, qui, on, com
negation with no

levels.name: Daily life
grammarAllowed: present indicative of all three conjugations, including the incoative -eix- type (serveixo, prefereixes)
tenir, haver, anar, fer, poder, voler in the present
possessives (el meu, la teva, els seus)
hi ha for existence
the periphrastic past (vaig menjar, vas anar) - the normal way to speak about the past in Catalan
cardinal numbers, days, telling the time
common prepositions a, de, en, amb, per, per a and the contractions al, del, pel

levels.name: Short stories
levels.sentenceLengthHint: max 10 words per sentence; at most one subordinate clause
grammarAllowed: imperfect indicative (parlava, tenia, era) for description and habit, contrasted with the periphrastic past for completed events
the perfect with haver (he menjat, hem arribat) for today's events
singular weak pronouns em, et, es, el, la, li and reflexive verbs (llevar-se, dir-se)
future indicative (parlaré, tindré)
comparatives and superlatives (més ... que, tan ... com, el més)
connectors però, perquè, quan, mentre
the personal a is NOT used in Catalan - never write 'veig a la Maria'

levels.name: Real texts
levels.sentenceLengthHint: max 14 words per sentence; subordinate clauses allowed
grammarAllowed: present subjunctive after voler que, esperar que, caldre que, quan + future reference
conditional (parlaria, voldria, m'agradaria) for politeness and hypothesis
plural and adverbial weak pronouns ens, us, els, hi, en - including en for partitives (en vull dos)
combined weak pronouns (me'l, l'hi, se'n) with correct apostrophes and hyphens
relative clauses with que, qui, on, el qual
the gerund for simultaneity (tot caminant) - never for consecutive actions
impersonal es (es parla català)

levels.name: Fluent reading
levels.sentenceLengthHint: max 18 words per sentence; multiple clauses allowed
grammarAllowed: imperfect subjunctive (parlés, tingués) and conditional sentences (si tingués temps, aniria)
pluperfect (havia arribat) and future perfect (haurà acabat)
passive with ser and the more idiomatic impersonal/pronominal alternatives
verbal periphrases (haver de, deure, estar a punt de, tornar a, acabar de)
discourse connectors (tanmateix, per tant, tot i que, malgrat que, en canvi)
nominalisation and more abstract vocabulary
register: distinguishing tu, vostè and vosaltres consistently

levels.name: Native texts
grammarAllowed: the full subjunctive system, including concessive and final clauses
the simple past (parlà, digué) as a literary register, alongside the everyday periphrastic past
fronting and other marked word orders for emphasis
idioms, phrasal expressions and figurative usage
formal and journalistic register, including impersonal constructions
regional awareness: Central Catalan is the standard here, but a reader may meet Valencian or Balearic forms
